subject: Quantile service-curve & burst-window capacity forecast
messages:
From: Daniel Hsu <daniel@zedhealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@zedhealth.com
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 08:17:00 -0800
Subject: Private deploy capacity: expected bursts and SLOs

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the intro call yesterday. We're moving towards a private VPC deployment for our inference workloads and need a firm capacity forecast and scaling plan from Redwood to include in our internal runbook. High-level asks:

- Sustained throughput target: 1,200 concurrent LLM requests (peak q50).
- Peak burst window: up to 3,600 concurrent requests for a 10-minute window (rare, q99).
- Latency SLO: p95 <= 250ms, p99 <= 700ms (end-to-end token latency).
- Typical request profile: 80 tokens output, average prompt 120 tokens; we expect ~60% cache-hit on common prefixes once warmed.

Can Redwood provide:
- A quantile service-curve (q50/q90/q99) with recommended GPU pool sizing and headroom assumptions.
- Suggested canary strategy for rolling out to our VPC.
- Network egress and MTU/throughput guidance for our NIC and fabric.

I'll attach our initial traffic trace (sanitized) and a simple runbook. Can we aim for a first cut by next Tuesday?

Thanks,
Daniel
Director of Platform
ZedHealth

Attachments: zedhealth_traffic_trace_sanitized.csv (referenced), zedhealth_runbook_draft.md

Appreciate the clear ask and the traces. We're on it. Quick clarifying questions before Marcus and infra scoping:

3) Do you require hard SLAs for p99, or is p99-best-effort with graceful fallback acceptable?

We'll prepare a QSC (quantile service curve) spreadsheet and a short canary playbook. Marcus will propose GPU pool sizing assumptions and Aditya will propose the NIC/network settings.

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>

Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Private deploy capacity: expected bursts and SLOs

Thanks — I pulled the trace and sketched a set of baseline assumptions. High-level summary (first-pass):

Assumptions
- Model: open-llama-70b-style variant (float16 runtime); per-token throughput ~= 80 tokens/sec/GPU under our optimized kernels for 1024 context.
- Average output: 80 tokens -> ~1.0s of GPU time per request (single-turn) w/o batching.
- Effective batching: with continuous-batching at q50 we expect batch sizes ~12-16, at q99 batch sizes drop to 1-4.
- KV cache hit: 60% overall, but depends on session stickiness. Cache hit reduces per-request compute by ~40%.

Sizing guidance (first cut)
- q50 sustained (1,200 concurrent): assume effective concurrency maps to GPU slots as concurrency / batch_scale. If q50 batch_scale=14 -> nominal GPU_count ~= ceil(1200 / (14 * 8)) = ~11 GPUs (8 streams per GPU). Add 30% headroom -> 15 GPUs.
- q90 sustained (2,000 concurrent): batch_scale=8 -> nominal GPUs ~= ceil(2000/(8*8)) = 32 GPUs -> add 25% headroom -> 40 GPUs.
- q99 burst (3,600 concurrent, 10m window): assume batch_scale=3 -> nominal GPUs ~= ceil(3600/(3*8)) = 150 GPUs. For a short window, we recommend staged burst capacity: reserve 60 GPUs dedicated + allow elastic burst to a partner-provided pool or cross-region fallbacks; otherwise contract for 150 GPUs if hard commit required.

Network & egress notes
- Anticipate ~1.2 Gbps per 100 concurrent requests (payloads + tokens). For 3,600 concurrent peak -> ~43 Gbps. Recommend 100GbE uplinks and jumbo frames (MTU 9000) end-to-end.
- Load balancer: use flow-aware NLB + upstream BGP anycast for cross-AZ resilience.

Canary suggestion
- Start with 10% traffic routed to private pool (15 GPUs) for 48 hours with synthetic spike test at 2x day traffic; monitor p95/p99 and queueing. Ramp to 50% (40 GPUs) then to 100% with burst-test window enabled.

Open items
- Confirm whether p99 must be hard SLA.
- Confirm average tokenization behavior (we assumed 80/120).

I'll drop the numbers into the spreadsheet and share.

—Marcus
Principal Inference Engineer
Redwood Inference

Marcus — thanks, this is helpful and more concrete than we expected. A few quick clarifications:

- The requests are a mix: ~70% single-turn, ~30% short multi-turn sessions that keep KV alive for ~3-4 turns. So your 60% hit rate seems reasonable.
- The 10-minute burst is campaign-driven and somewhat predictable (we can give you a schedule for the first 6 months).
- For p99: it's important for patient-facing flows, but procurement will accept a tiered SLA (p95 contractual, p99 best-effort).

Two asks:
1) Can you include a simple thermal/operational headroom note (we run in on-prem metal racks with limited cooling)?
2) We need a note on eBPF or traffic shaping at the host level — can Redwood recommend QoS knobs to avoid noisy neighbor impact?

If you can fold that into the EOD draft that would be great.

Daniel

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Private deploy capacity: expected bursts and SLOs

Quick infra addendum on host/network and thermal ops:

Host/network recommendations
- NIC: dual 100GbE with LACP; enable jumbo frames MTU=9000 and set rx/tx ring sizes to 4096.
- Kernel: tune SO_REUSEPORT and set net.core.somaxconn=4096; tcp_tw_reuse=1.
- QoS: use tc + eBPF policing to reserve 60% of NIC for inference traffic, keep 30% for control plane and 10% for burst absorb. Implement fq_codel qdisc with per-flow rate caps to reduce head-of-line blocking.
- LB: front with an L4 NLB that supports flow-stickiness and connection draining during canary rollouts.

Thermal / operational headroom
- Racking density: expect ~3-4 kW per rack for Gpus at this scale. Recommend not exceeding 80% rack power draw for sustained workloads; reserve 20% for thermal headroom.
- If bursts are common, implement staggered fan profiles and an inlet-temperature alarm tied to autoscale triggers.

Elastic burst suggestion
- If procurement won't commit to 150 GPUs, recommend hybrid burst: 60 dedicated GPUs + contract for spot/dedicated burst up to additional 120 GPUs with a partner pool or cloud bridging. This reduces on-prem cooling and floor-space commitments.

I'll annotate the capacity spreadsheet with these knobs.

—Aditya
SRE, Redwood Inference

Thanks everyone — consolidated summary and next steps below.

Summary decisions (first draft)
- Baseline private GPU pool: 15 GPUs for initial q50 traffic (covers earliest canary).
- Mid ramp target: 40 GPUs to handle q90 sustained loads.
- Burst plan: reserve 60 GPUs on-prem + elastic burst to partner pool up to 120 GPUs for 10-minute campaign windows. Procurement to confirm acceptable burst contract.
- Network: dual 100GbE, MTU 9000, jumbo frames, eBPF policing to reserve inference bandwidth.
- Canaries: 10% -> 50% -> 100% ramp, with synthetic spike test at each stage.
- SLA: p95 contractual, p99 best-effort (per Daniel's acceptance).

Action items
- Redwood: finalize qsc spreadsheet with the numeric derivations and thermal ops notes and share Drive folder link (I will upload v2). Owner: Marcus / Aditya. Due: 2026-11-24 EOD PT.
- ZedHealth: share campaign schedule for the first 6 months so we can plan burst reservations. Owner: Daniel. Due: 2026-11-26.
- Procurement (ZedHealth): confirm whether hybrid burst contract acceptable; share preferred vendor IDs if yes. Due: 2026-11-30.

Links and artifacts
